Rashi on Ketubot 57a:10:1.hebrew: נותנין לבתולה - זמן לכניסתה לחופה, מיום שתבעה הבעל לאחר שקידשה, להזהירה על עסקי חופה, להכין תכשיטיה:
Rashi on Ketubot 57a:10:1.english: One gives a virgin - [They give her] time for her entry into the wedding canopy, from the day the husband demanded [to marry] her after he betrothed her, to notify her regarding the affairs of the wedding canopy, to prepare her jewelry.

Rashi on Ketubot 57a:10:2.english: To provide for herself - With adornments.

Rashi on Ketubot 57a:10:3.english: To prepare himself - With the needs of the [wedding] feast and the wedding canopy.

Rashi on Ketubot 57a:10:4.hebrew: ולאלמנה ל' יום - שאינה טורחת כל כך בתכשיטין, שכבר יש בידה:
Rashi on Ketubot 57a:10:4.english: And for a widow, thirty days - Because she does not trouble herself so much with ornaments, as she already has [some] in her possession.

Rashi on Ketubot 57a:10:5.hebrew: ולא נישאו - שהבעלים מעכבין, ואיידי דתנא רישא בדידהי, תנא סיפא נמי בדידהי:
Rashi on Ketubot 57a:10:5.english: And they were not married - [Meaning] that the husbands are delaying [the marriage]. And since [the Tanna] taught the first clause concerning them [the women], he taught the latter clause concerning them as well.

Rashi on Ketubot 57a:10:6.hebrew: ואוכלת בתרומה - אם כהן הוא והיא ישראלית, שמשעה שקידשה אוכלת בתרומה מן התורה כדמפרש בגמרא, ורבנן גזור עד השתא:
Rashi on Ketubot 57a:10:6.english: And she may partake of terumah - If he is a priest and she is an Israelite [woman], for from the moment he betrothed her she may partake of terumah by Torah law, as the Gemara explains, and the Rabbis decreed [a prohibition] until now.

Rashi on Ketubot 57a:11:1.hebrew: נותנין לה הכל תרומה - אם ירצה, וכשיגיעו ימי טומאתה תמכרנה ותקח חולין:
Rashi on Ketubot 57a:11:1.english: They give her all teruma - If he wishes, and when the days of her [ritual] impurity arrive, she sells it and buys non-sacred [food].

Rashi on Ketubot 57a:11:2.english: Half non-sacred food - To eat during the days of her [ritual] impurity.

Rashi on Ketubot 57a:12:1.hebrew: היבם אינו מאכיל בתרומה - בעודה שומרת יבם, וטעמא יליף בגמרא:
Rashi on Ketubot 57a:12:1.english: The yavam does not enable [her] to eat teruma - while she is awaiting the yavam, and the reason is derived in the Gemara.

Rashi on Ketubot 57a:12:2.hebrew: עשתה ששה חדשים בפני הבעל - מהנך שנים עשר חדש הקבועים לה משתבעה הבעל, או אפילו כולם בפני הבעל ואחד בפני היבם, אע"ג דרובא בפני הבעל, סוף סוף לא נתחייב במזונותיה בחייו. והוא הדין נמי אם נתחייב בחייו, לא אכלה משמת, דקניין הבעל פקע; אלא דאי כולם בפני הבעל, הוה אכלה מיהא בחייו:
Rashi on Ketubot 57a:12:2.english: If she completed six months under the aegis of the husband - Of those twelve months that are fixed for her from when the husband claimed her [for marriage]; or even [if she completed] all of them under the aegis of the husband and one [day] under the aegis of the yavam, even though the majority [of the time] was under the aegis of the husband, ultimately he did not become obligated in her sustenance during his lifetime. And the same law [applies] as well if he did become obligated during his lifetime: she does not partake [of teruma] once he has died, for the acquisition of the husband has lapsed; rather, if all of them [had been] under the aegis of the husband, she would at least have partaken during his lifetime.

Rashi on Ketubot 57a:12:3.hebrew: או כולן בפני היבם - בגמרא פריך עלה, למאי תניא:
Rashi on Ketubot 57a:12:3.english: Or all of them before the yavam - In the Gemara, it asks regarding this: For what [purpose] was it taught?

Rashi on Ketubot 57a:13:1.english: This is the initial mishnah - That once the time [for marriage] has arrived, she eats terumah.

Rashi on Ketubot 57a:1:1.english: Her marriage contract was lost - The document of her marriage contract.

Rashi on Ketubot 57a:1:2.hebrew: זו דברי ר"מ - דאמר לעיל כל הפוחת לבתולה ממאתים, ואפי' בתנאה והתנאי בטל, קרי לה בעילת זנות משום דלא סמכא דעתה. והכא נמי, לר"מ הוא דאסור לשהות אשה שאבדה שטר כתובתה, ואפי' אית לה דלא מפסדא בהכי, דגביא בתנאי ב"ד, מיהא לא סמכא דעתה, דאמרה: כי תבענא ליה, אמר פרעתיך. הלכך, בעילת זנות היא:
Rashi on Ketubot 57a:1:2.english: This is the statement of Rabbi Meir - Who said above [that] anyone who diminishes [the marriage contract] of a virgin from two hundred [zuz] — even by stipulation, and the stipulation is void — calls it licentious intercourse, because she is not confident [in her marriage]. And here too, it is according to Rabbi Meir that it is forbidden to remain [married to] a woman whose marriage contract document was lost; and even though she has [the assurance] that she does not lose out by this, since she collects by the court's stipulation, nevertheless she is not confident, for she says [to herself], 'When I claim [it] from him, he will say, "I already paid you."' Therefore, it is licentious intercourse.

Rashi on Ketubot 57a:2:1.english: But the Sages say, etc. - For we need not be concerned about [her] reliance of mind, such that [it] would be promiscuous intercourse.

Rashi on Ketubot 57a:2:2.english: In his decrees - In a matter where he is stringent beyond Torah law in [matters of] prohibition and permission, by way of a decree of their [i.e., the Sages'] words.

Rashi on Ketubot 57a:2:3.hebrew: אי הכי זיל כתוב לה - כתובה אחריתי. והא דאמרינן לעיל (כתובות דף נא.): לא כתב לה כתובה, בתולה גובה מאתים, ואוקמינן כר"מ — התם במקום שאין כותבין כתובה, דכולהו אתנאי קא סמכי. אי נמי, במקום שכותבין, וגובה לר"מ; מיהו, בעילת זנות באיסור היא:
Rashi on Ketubot 57a:2:3.english: If so, go [and] write her - another marriage contract. And [as for] that which we said earlier (Ketubot 51a): "[If] he did not write a marriage contract for her, a virgin collects two hundred [zuz]," and we established it in accordance with Rabbi Meir — there [it is speaking] of a place where they do not write a marriage contract, for everyone relies on the [court] stipulation. Alternatively, [it is speaking] of a place where they do write [a marriage contract], and she collects according to Rabbi Meir; however, [cohabiting without one] is promiscuous intercourse, [which is] forbidden.

Rashi on Ketubot 57a:3:1.hebrew: מחלוקת - דרבי יהודה ור' יוסי, דאמר ר' יהודה: על פה לאו תנאה הוא, ור' יוסי סבר: תנאה קיים:
Rashi on Ketubot 57a:3:1.english: Dispute - Of Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Yosei, as Rabbi Yehuda says [that a stipulation made] orally is not a [valid] condition, and Rabbi Yosei holds [that] the condition stands.

Rashi on Ketubot 57a:3:2.english: At the beginning - [The Gemara] explains below: the beginning of what?

Rashi on Ketubot 57a:3:3.hebrew: דברי הכל אינה מוחלת - שכבר זכתה, ואמירתה לאו כלום, אלא א"כ כתבה שובר "התקבלתי":
Rashi on Ketubot 57a:3:3.english: All agree [that] she cannot waive [it] - For she has already acquired [her ketubah], and her [verbal] statement is nothing unless she wrote a receipt [stating], "I have received [it]."

Rashi on Ketubot 57a:4:1.hebrew: תחלת חופה ומאי סוף סוף ביאה - וה"ק: מתחלת חופה ועד סוף חופה פליגי בה רבי יהודה ור' יוסי, אבל משבא עליה מודה ר' יוסי דאין בדבריו כלום:
Rashi on Ketubot 57a:4:1.english: [The] beginning of [the] bridal canopy, and what is [meant by] "end"? The end of intercourse - And this is what he is saying: from the beginning of [the] bridal canopy until the end of [the] bridal canopy, Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Yosei disagree about it; however, once he has engaged in intercourse with her, Rabbi Yosei concedes that there is nothing in his words.

Rashi on Ketubot 57a:4:2.hebrew: וכי אמינא אנא בין בזו בין בזו מחלוקת - לאו אסוף דרבי יהושע קאמינא, אלא אסוף חופה, דהיא קודם ביאה:
Rashi on Ketubot 57a:4:2.english: And when I said, "Both in this [case] and in that [case] there is a dispute" - I was not referring to the "end" of Rabbi Yehoshua [ben Levi], rather to the end of the wedding canopy, which is before intercourse.

Rashi on Ketubot 57a:6:1.hebrew: אמר רב פפא אי לאו דאמר כו' - אנא לא הוה ניחא לי לפרושי מילתייהו הכי, דרבי יוחנן ור' יהושע לא ליפלגו ורב דימי ורבין ניפלגו בדרבי יהושע. אלא הכי הוה אמינא: רבי יוחנן ור' יהושע בן לוי פליגי, דאההוא סוף דקאמר רבי יהושע בן לוי דברי הכל אינה מוחלת, אתא רבי יוחנן למימר אף בזו מחלוקת, דרב דימי ורבין לא פליגי בדרבי יהושע. והכי הוה מפרישנא לדרב דימי: אמר רבי יהושע, מחלוקת בתחלת ביאה דהיא סוף חופה, אבל בסוף ביאה דברי הכל אינה מוחלת; ורבי יוחנן פליג עליה, דאפילו בסוף ביאה נמי פליגי. וכי אתא רבין, אמר רבי יהושע בן לוי: מחלוקת בסוף חופה — והיא תחלת ביאה דקאמר נמי רב דימי — אבל בתחלת חופה דברי הכל מוחלת. אבל השתא דפריש רבי אבהו לדרב דימי, דבין לרבי יוחנן ובין לרבי יהושע בן לוי פליגי רבי יוסי ורבי יהודה בתחלת חופה ובסוף חופה, על כרחך פליגא דרבין אדרב דימי, דהא אמר רבין בתחלת חופה ד"ה מוחלת:
Rashi on Ketubot 57a:6:1.english: Rav Pappa said: Had [Rabbi Abbahu] not said, etc. - It would not have been pleasing to me to explain their words in this way, [namely,] that Rabbi Yoḥanan and Rabbi Yehoshua do not disagree, while Rav Dimi and Ravin disagree regarding [the view of] Rabbi Yehoshua. Rather, this is what I would have said: Rabbi Yoḥanan and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi disagree — for regarding that end [stage] about which Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said that all agree she does not waive [her rights], Rabbi Yoḥanan came to say that even in this [case] there is a dispute — such that Rav Dimi and Ravin do not disagree regarding [the view of] Rabbi Yehoshua. And this is how I would have explained [the statement of] Rav Dimi: Rabbi Yehoshua said, the dispute is at the beginning of cohabitation, which is the end of the wedding canopy, whereas at the end of cohabitation all agree she does not waive [her rights]; and Rabbi Yoḥanan disagrees with him, [holding] that even at the end of cohabitation they also disagree. And when Ravin came, he said [in the name of] Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi: The dispute is at the end of the wedding canopy — which is [the same as] the beginning of cohabitation that Rav Dimi also spoke of — whereas at the beginning of the wedding canopy all agree she waives [her rights]. But now that Rabbi Abbahu has explained [the statement of] Rav Dimi [to mean] that according to both Rabbi Yoḥanan and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Yehudah disagree both at the beginning of the wedding canopy and at the end of the wedding canopy, perforce [the statement of] Ravin disagrees with [that of] Rav Dimi, for Ravin said that at the beginning of the wedding canopy all agree she waives [her rights].

Rashi on Ketubot 57a:8:1.hebrew: מאי קמ"ל - בהא דאמר אי לאו דקאמר רבי אבהו כו'? האמר רבי אבהו, ואיהו לא בעי לאיפלוגי עליה, ולמאי הלכתא אשמועינן דאי לא אמרה רבי אבהו הוה ניחא ליה לדידיה לפרושי בענין אחר:
Rashi on Ketubot 57a:8:1.english: What is he teaching us - by this that he said, "Had Rabbi Abbahu not said, etc."? Why, Rabbi Abbahu [already] said it, and he [Rav Pappa] does not wish to disagree with him; so for what halakhic purpose did he inform us that had Rabbi Abbahu not said it, he himself would have preferred to explain [it] in another way?

Rashi on Ketubot 57a:9:1.hebrew: הא קמ"ל - דהיכא דאשכחן אמוראי דפליגי אהדדי כל חד אליבא דנפשיה, ותרי אמוראי אחריני דפליגי בפלוגתא דהנך אמוראי, ואית לן לפרושי מילתא בתרי לישני — חדא מינייהו מיפלגי תרי אמוראי אליבא דנפשייהו, שכל אחד אומר סברא שלו, כגון רבי יוחנן ורבי יהושע, ואינך תרי אמוראי [אליבא דחד] לא מיפלגי אלא אמרי חדא מלתא; וחדא מן לישנא מיפלגי תרי אמוראי אליבא דחד, כגון רב דימי ורבין, ומשויא מלתא דתרי אמוראי קמאי חדא מלתא — שבקינן ההיא לישנא דמיפלגי תרי אמוראי אליבא דחד, ונקטינן ההיא דמיפלגי תרי אמוראי אליבא דנפשייהו. דכי פליגי תרי אליבא דחד — מר אמר הכי אמר פלוני, ומר אמר הכי אמר פלוני — חד מינייהו משקר. אבל כי פליגי תרי אמוראי בדין או באיסור והיתר, כל חד אמר הכי מיסתבר טעמא — אין כאן שקר. כל חד וחד סברא דידיה קאמר: מר יהיב טעמא להיתירא, ומר יהיב טעמא לאיסורא; מר מדמי מילתא למילתא הכי, ומר מדמי ליה בעניינא אחרינא. ואיכא למימר אלו ואלו דברי אלהים חיים הם: זימנין דשייך האי טעמא, וזימנין דשייך האי טעמא, שהטעם מתהפך לפי שינוי הדברים בשינוי מועט:
Rashi on Ketubot 57a:9:1.english: This [is what] it teaches us - That wherever we find amora'im who disagree with one another, each according to his own [reasoning], and two other amora'im who disagree about the dispute of those amora'im, and we have to explain the matter in two versions — one of them [is that] two amora'im disagree according to themselves, as each one states his own reasoning, such as Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Yehoshua, and the other two amora'im [according to one] do not disagree, rather they say one thing; and one of the versions [is that] two amora'im disagree according to one [authority], such as Rav Dimi and Ravin, and it makes the statement of the first two amora'im one thing — we set aside that version where two amora'im disagree according to one, and we adopt that [version] where two amora'im disagree according to themselves. For when two disagree according to one — one says "so said so-and-so," and one says "so said so-and-so" — one of them is lying. However, when two amora'im disagree in a matter of law or in [a matter of] what is forbidden and permitted, each one saying "so does the reasoning appear," there is no falsehood here. Each and every one states his own reasoning: one gives a reason for permitting, and one gives a reason for forbidding; one compares a matter to [another] matter in this way, and one compares it in another respect. And it is possible to say [that] "both these and those are the words of the living God": at times this reason is applicable, and at times that reason is applicable, for the reason reverses according to a change in the circumstances, [even] with a slight change.

Tosafot on Ketubot 57a:12:1.hebrew: ואפילו כולן בפני הבעל חוץ מיום אחד אינה אוכלת - פירש בקונטרס דהוא הדין אפילו כולם בפני הבעל לא אכלה משמת, ד"קנין כספו" פקע ליה, אלא דאי כולן בפני הבעל הוה אכלה מיהא בחייו. ולר"ת נראה דהך דרשא דדריש בגמרא: "קנין כספו" אמר רחמנא והאי קנין דאחיו הוא — אסמכתא בעלמא הוא, דמדאורייתא מיכל אכלה, ולפי משנה ראשונה היכא דאכלה בחיי הבעל אוכלת נמי בזיקת היבם, מדקתני: "ואפי' כולם בפני הבעל חוץ מיום אחד" — משמע: הא כולן בפני הבעל אוכלת. ועוד, דתנן בפרקין בסדר משנת ירושלמית: "הגיע זמן ולא נשאו, או שמתו בעליהן — אוכלות משלו ואוכלות בתרומה", משמע כשמתו בעליהן שהיבם מאכילן בלא ביאה, דומיא דהגעת זמן דמיירי בלא נשאו, דאי אחר ביאה — פשיטא, דאשתו גמורה היא. ועוד מביא ראיה מדתניא בתוספתא: "זו משנה ראשונה; רבותינו אמרו: אין האשה אוכלת בתרומה עד שתכנס לחופה, ולא היבמה עד שתיבעל". והיינו טעמא דמשנה ראשונה דכשלא אכלה בחיי הבעל אינה אוכלת, דהא איכא למיחש לסימפון ולשמא תשקה, דהא כיון דלא הגיע זמן בחיי הבעל לא בדק לה, דאינו חייב במזונותיה אלא א"כ עמד בדין וברח כדאמרינן בהחולץ (יבמות דף מא:), ולא מייחד לה דוכתא — וטעמא משום שאין דרך לאחר, אלא מיד הוא רגיל או לחלוץ או לייבם, לכך לא תקנו לה מזונות מיבם כמו שתקנו מזונות בהגעת זמן דבעל. אבל כשאכלה בחיי הבעל — תו ליכא למיחש לסימפון, ולשמא תשקה נמי ליכא למיחש, דכיון דהגיע זמן מייחד לה דוכתא בבית אביה, מסתמא אוכלת שם בכל שעה ואינה זזה ממקומה. וא"ת: ומאחר דמדאורייתא אכלה כשנפלה מן הנשואין, למה אסורה למשנה אחרונה עד שתיבעל? הא ליכא למיחש לסימפון, שכבר נבדקה בדיקת פנים! ויש לומר: דמאחר שאסרו ארוסה שהגיע זמנה, אסרו נמי ביבמה משום דמיחלפא בה, ששתיהן זמן כניסתן לאלתר. אבל ק"ק: אי חשיבא יבמה "קנין כספו" דיבם, הא דקאמר ביבמות בפרק אלמנה (דף סז: ושם) גבי הא דתנן "היבם פוסל ואינו מאכיל": אי בת כהן לישראל היא, פסיל לה, "ושבה אל בית אביה" כו' — ה"ל למימר דהא קנייה, כדקאמר התם גבי אירוסין! ויש לומר: ד"ושבה אל בית אביה" אתא למיפסל בת כהן לישראל, למידק הא מעיקרא לא אכלה כדאמר התם (דף סח.), א"כ לא אייתר לשומרת יבם. אלא הכי קאמר: "ושבה" כתיב, כלומר: דווקא אותה ששבה אל בית אביה, אבל זאת שזקוקה ליבם אינה שבה, שהרי חשובה כאילו קנויה לו:
Tosafot on Ketubot 57a:12:1.english: And even [if she completed] all of them under the aegis of the husband except for one day, she may not partake [of terumah] - Rashi explained that the same law [applies] even [if she completed] all of them under the aegis of the husband: she may not partake once he dies, because [his] "acquisition of his money" has lapsed; rather, [the Mishnah phrased it this way because] if [she completed] all of them under the aegis of the husband, she would at least have partaken during his lifetime. And to Rabbeinu Tam it appears that this exposition that the Gemara expounds — "the Merciful One said 'acquisition of his money,' and this [woman] is the acquisition of his brother" — is merely an asmakhta [a scriptural support for a rabbinic law], for by Torah law she indeed partakes [of terumah]. And according to the early Mishnah, where she partook during the husband's lifetime, she also partakes through the levirate bond of the yavam, since [the Mishnah] teaches, "And even [if she completed] all of them under the aegis of the husband except for one day," which implies: [if she completed] all of them under the aegis of the husband, she does partake. Furthermore, we learned in our chapter in the order of the Jerusalem Mishnah: "When the time arrived and they were not married, or if their husbands died, they partake of his [food] and they partake of terumah" — which implies that when their husbands died, the yavam enables them to partake without marital relations, similar to the arrival of the time, which refers to [a case where] they were not married; for if [it referred to] after marital relations, it is obvious, as she is his full-fledged wife. Furthermore, [Rabbeinu Tam] brings a proof from that which was taught in the Tosefta: "This is the early Mishnah; our Rabbis said: A woman does not partake of terumah until she enters the wedding canopy, nor does a yevamah until she has marital relations." And this is the reason of the early Mishnah: when she did not partake during the husband's lifetime, she does not partake [under the yavam], because there is [reason] to be concerned about a disqualifying blemish (simpon) and lest she pour [terumah for her family] — for since the time had not arrived during the husband's lifetime, he did not examine her, as [the yavam] is not obligated to provide her sustenance unless he stood in court and fled, as we say in [chapter] HaCholetz (Yevamot 41b), and he does not designate a [specific] place for her. And the reason is that it is not customary to delay, rather he is accustomed either to perform chalitzah or to perform yibum immediately; therefore they did not institute sustenance for her from the yavam as they instituted sustenance upon the arrival of the time for a husband. However, when she [already] partook during the husband's lifetime, there is no longer [reason] to be concerned about a blemish, and there is also no [reason] to be concerned about lest she pour [for her family], because since the time arrived, he designates a place for her in her father's house, [so] presumably she eats there at all times and does not move from her place. And if you say: Since by Torah law she partakes when she fell [into levirate marriage] from full marriage (nisu'in), why is she forbidden according to the later Mishnah until she has marital relations? Surely there is no [reason] to be concerned about a blemish, as she was already examined in an intimate examination! One can say: Since they forbade a betrothed woman whose time had arrived, they also forbade a yevamah because she is confused with her, as for both of them the time of their entry [into marriage] is immediate. However, it is somewhat difficult: if a yevamah is considered the "acquisition of his money" of the yavam, [then regarding] that which [the Gemara] says in Yevamot in chapter Almanah (67b and there [elsewhere]) concerning that which we learned, "The yavam disqualifies [her] and does not enable [her] to partake": if she is the daughter of a kohen [married] to an Israelite, he disqualifies her, [from the verse] "'and she returns to her father's house,' etc." — it should have said, "for he has acquired her," just as it says there regarding betrothal! One can say that [since the verse] "and she returns to her father's house" comes to disqualify the daughter of a kohen [married] to an Israelite — to infer that initially she did not partake, as it says there (68a) — if so, it is not superfluous for a shomeret yavam [a woman awaiting levirate marriage]. Rather, this is what it is saying: "and she returns" is written, meaning specifically one who returns to her father's house [may partake], whereas this one who is bound to the yavam has not returned, for she is considered as though acquired by him.

Tosafot on Ketubot 57a:2:1.hebrew: שתים ושלש שנים - אין לדקדק כאן: "השתא שלש מותר, שתים מיבעיא?" — דדלמא שתים ושלש ואפי' טובא, כדאמרי אינשי, כדמשני בפרק מפנין (שבת קכז.); ואין להאריך כאן:
Tosafot on Ketubot 57a:2:1.english: Two or three years - One should not scrutinize [the phrasing] here [and ask]: "Now [that] three [years] are permitted, is there a question about two?" — for perhaps [it means] "two or three, and even many," as people say, as [the Gemara] answers in the chapter [entitled] Mefanin (Shabbat 127a); and there is no [need] to elaborate here.

Tosafot on Ketubot 57a:9:1.hebrew: ולא פליגי תרי גברי אליבא דחד גברא - וא"ת: ומאי נפקא מינה? דהשתא נמי פליגי ר' יוחנן ור' יהושע ב"ל אליבא דחד תנא, ומה לי תרי אמוראי אליבא דחד אמורא ומה לי אליבא דחד תנא? וי"ל: דאי פליגי ר' יוחנן ור' יהושע בן לוי אליבא דחד תנא — לא חיישינן, דבסברא הוא דפליגי ולא טעו בשמועתם; אבל אי פליגי רבין ורב דימי בדברי רבי יוחנן ורבי יהושע בן לוי, שזה אומר: "כך אמר", וזה אומר: "כך אמר" — אחד מהם טעה בשמועתו:
Tosafot on Ketubot 57a:9:1.english: And two men do not disagree according to one man - And if you say: What is the practical difference? For even now, Rabbi Yoḥanan and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi disagree according to one tanna, and what [difference is it] to me [whether] two amora’im [disagree] according to one amora, and what [difference is it] to me [whether they disagree] according to one tanna? And one can say: That if Rabbi Yoḥanan and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi disagree according to one tanna, we are not concerned, for it is in [logical] reasoning that they disagree, and they did not err in their received tradition; but if Ravin and Rav Dimi disagree regarding the words of Rabbi Yoḥanan and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, where this one says, "Thus he said," and that one says, "Thus he said" — one of them erred in his received tradition.
